review_notes: I read the whole file and the related declarations it uses (the Mathlib affine-open and PrimeSpectrum API was not re-opened in detail). I looked for nontrivial reasoning repeated across proofs. I found two candidates. The first is the embedding of Z(p) into closure {x} through fromSpec, which is built separately in zeroLocus_le_closure and closure_le. The second is the "height is finite, so it is a natural number, and height + quotient dimension = dimension" computation, which is done once for p and once for a maximal ideal m in chart_numbers. I did not find other substantial duplication. The repeated n'=n and h'=h casts are too short to report. I could not compile any proposed replacement, so the proof sketches are untested.

findings.declaration: zeroLocus_le_closure / closure_le (embedding of Z(p) into closure {x} via fromSpec)
findings.problem: Both proofs rebuild the same map. It sends q in zeroLocus(primeIdealOf x) to hU.fromSpec q in closure {x}. Each one separately proves membership in the closure, using fromSpec_mem_closure together with asIdeal_le_asIdeal. Each one also separately proves that the codomain restriction of fromSpec ∘ val is an embedding. zeroLocus_le_closure does this through the generic helper topologicalKrullDim_le_of_isEmbedding_image, which itself redoes the codRestrict-of-inducing argument. closure_le does it by hand with a local `g` and `hgemb`. The shared construction is written twice, so any change to the closure-membership argument has to be made in two places.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma in the Charts section, taking {X : Scheme.{u}} {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U). It defines `zeroLocusToClosure hU x hx : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ((hU.primeIdealOf ⟨x,hx⟩).asIdeal : Set Γ(X,U)) → closure ({x} : Set X)`, sending q to ⟨hU.fromSpec q.1, fromSpec_mem_closure hU x hx q.1 ((PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal_le_asIdeal _ _).mp q.2)⟩. It also proves `IsEmbedding (zeroLocusToClosure hU x hx)` by `((hU.fromSpec.isOpenEmbedding.isEmbedding).comp IsEmbedding.subtypeVal).codRestrict _ _`. Optionally it proves the range equation `Set.range _ = Subtype.val ⁻¹' (U : Set X)`, which is currently inlined as `hrange`. After that, zeroLocus_le_closure becomes `Topology.IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le (zeroLocusToClosure_isEmbedding hU x hx).isInducing`. This removes both the helper `topologicalKrullDim_le_of_isEmbedding_image` and its image-subset side goal. In closure_le, `g`, `hgemb` and `hrange` become uses of the shared definition and lemmas, giving `hg : IsOpenEmbedding (zeroLocusToClosure hU' x hxU')`. The hypotheses are unchanged: both uses already work with an affine open U/U' containing x and the same ambient imports.
findings.benefit: The Z(p) → closure {x} chart map is defined and shown to be an embedding once. The two proofs shrink to short uses of it. closure_le then reads as the chart-covering argument, and zeroLocus_le_closure as a one-line consequence of the embedding.

findings.declaration: chart_numbers (finite-height and dimension formula for p and for a maximal ideal m)
findings.problem: The proof runs the same argument twice. For an ideal I of the finite-type k-algebra Γ(X,U), it applies Ideal.height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_eq_ringKrullDim_of_finiteType and then shows I.height ≠ ⊤ via FiniteHeight and Ideal.height_ne_top. It then extracts a natural number with ENat.ne_top_iff_exists. This happens once for p (lines 114-119) and again for the maximal ideal m (lines 124-133). The 'height is a natural number h with h + dim(A/I) = dim A' step is pasted rather than stated once, which makes the already long proof harder to follow.
findings.proposed_change: Prove a local lemma. Its hypotheses are [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] and I : Ideal A with I.IsPrime. Its conclusion is `∃ h : ℕ, I.height = h ∧ ((h : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) + ringKrullDim (A ⧸ I) = ringKrullDim A`. The proof applies the finite-type height formula to `I`. It then uses `Ideal.height_ne_top` with `IsNoetherianRing` and `Ideal.IsPrime.ne_top`. Finally it uses `ENat.ne_top_iff_exists` and rewrites. In chart_numbers, apply it to p to get h, and apply it to m, together with ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field on A⧸m, to get n. This replaces lines 114-133.
findings.benefit: The finite-height extraction is stated once as a named fact, and chart_numbers is shorter. It also becomes clear that n and h come from the same mechanism applied to a maximal and a prime ideal.
